strengths: Strong own-site visibility at 72.5%, indicating the brand is already being surfaced in AI answers.
Clear differentiation around stablecoins plus bank rails, which matches the use cases AI tends to discuss.
Product breadth is compelling: accounts, payments, invoicing, portfolios, and approvals in one workflow.
The site directly addresses a real pain point AI recognizes: reconciliation and approval friction across tools.
Lisk has 0.0% unprompted recall in brand-free category queries, while the platforms above own the visible share of voice.
opportunities: Leverage the fact that Base is surfacing at 90.0% to create more adjacent content around treasury, onchain operations, and digital money workflows.
Use comparison content against Bill.com, Ramp, Safe, and Fireblocks to intercept AI citations in common buyer journeys.
Strengthen category language around 'treasury' and 'payments' since these are dominant AI keywords.
Expand third-party mentions and citations to reduce dependence on generic competitors like Bill.com, which is currently the top cited source.
gaps: AI search does not consistently pick up the site's brand-specific language such as 'one workspace' or 'modern money'.
The site is less visible than Base and only moderately visible versus Ramp, Safe, and Fireblocks in adjacent categories.
Bill.com dominates source citations (17 mentions), suggesting the category association still leans toward incumbent AP/payments tools.
The homepage's integrated product story is stronger than the AI's current understanding of the brand's category position.
